purpose: Zanamivir is used to treat influenza (the flu) in adults and children who have had symptoms for no more than 2 days. It can also be used to help prevent the flu if you have been around someone who is sick. It works best when started as soon as possible after flu symptoms begin.
how_it_works: The flu virus has a protein on its surface called neuraminidase that helps it spread from cell to cell in your body. Zanamivir blocks this protein so the virus cannot escape infected cells and spread further. This helps stop the flu from getting worse and shortens how long you feel sick.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, dizziness, nausea, diarrhea, and cough or throat irritation from the inhaled powder. These are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: If you have asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), zanamivir can cause serious breathing problems, including sudden bronchospasm, and is generally NOT recommended for you. Always have a fast-acting rescue inhaler nearby if your doctor does prescribe it. Stop using it and call your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing. In rare cases, people — especially children — have had unusual behavior or confusion while taking flu antivirals. Tell your doctor right away if this happens.
typical_dosing: For treating the flu: you inhale 2 puffs (10 mg total) twice a day for 5 days, about 12 hours apart. For preventing the flu: you inhale 2 puffs once a day for 10 days if exposed to someone with the flu, or up to 28 days during a community outbreak. It is inhaled using a special device called a Diskhaler — your pharmacist can show you exactly how to use it.
